title: Chrono-Sphere Arena: Time-Warp Bowling
description: The player controls a glowing ShaderBall on a futuristic lane, aiming and launching it toward an arrangement of Rolex watches standing upright as bowling pins. Each knocked-down watch freezes a visible countdown timer, and the player must clear all pins across multiple rounds while managing power, spin, and angle to beat a par score.
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a 3D bowling-style game called Chrono-Sphere Arena. Load ShaderBall2.glb as the bowling ball and rolex.glb as the pins.

SCENE SETUP: Build a dark metallic bowling lane (30 units long, 4 units wide) with emissive neon edge strips. Place 6 Rolex watches scaled appropriately and standing upright in a triangular pin formation (1-2-3 rows) at the far end. Position the ShaderBall at the near end as the player's ball. Use a perspective camera starting behind the ball at a slight elevated angle. Add ambient light, a directional light, and point lights near the pins for dramatic effect.

INTERACTION STEPS (6-8 required): 1) Player clicks a 'Start Round' button to begin (round counter 1-3 displayed in HTML overlay). 2) Player drags left/right on the lane to set lateral aim position (clamped within lane bounds, show a visible aim guide line). 3) Player uses a vertical slider or mouse-drag-up gesture to set launch power (range 5-30, displayed numerically). 4) Player presses a 'Spin' toggle button cycling through Left/None/Right spin modes. 5) Player clicks 'Launch' to fire the ball down the lane with physics-based animation (translate + optional curve based on spin). 6) Detect collisions between ball and watches using bounding-box checks; knocked pins rotate and fall with animation. 7) Update and display score (each pin = 10 points, strike bonus = 20). 8) After ball reaches end, reset ball position for next round; after 3 rounds show final score overlay with 'Play Again' button.

VALIDATION: Clamp aim within lane width. Validate power is between 5-30. Prevent launch if round is not active. Disable controls during ball animation. Track pin states to avoid double-counting. All parameters must be validated before launch proceeds. Use requestAnimationFrame for smooth animation. Ensure both GLB models are visible and central to gameplay.
